thread:
Alex: Morning — quick async standup for the train. What I did: finished the metrics tagging change and landed the feature flag. What Iound: nightly integration flaked on the 'session-restore' test twice. Action: re-running CI now.
Priya: Thx. Heads-up: I merged the latency-stats backport into release/x and opened a cherry-pick PR (#452) for stable-rail. Needs one more review + approvals.
Jorge: On the flake — I saw similar in canary earlier. It's the teardown race in TestSessionHandler. Adding a small sleep worked locally but not ideal. I can try the mutex fix and send a tiny PR.
Tina: I can review #452 this morning. Also: do we want to include the quantization config tweak in this cut? It's a small perf win but touches runtime files.
Alex: Tina — prefer to hold runtime tweaks unless it's a blocker. We can ship them in the next minor unless you think it reduces error rate.
Tina: It reduces p99 by ~7% in our perf harness, but it did cause one edge-case failure on older CUDA drivers. Not worth risking the train. I'll queue it for next train.
Sam: I pinged infra to increase runner concurrency for the next hour to speed up re-runs. If CI stays flaky after Jorge's fix, maybe we ask for a short freeze and do a manual backport.
Priya: For the cherry list: confirmed picks are #452 (latency-stats), #460 (docs fix), and #468 (security label). I've listed owners in the PR descriptions.
Jorge: I'll open the tiny mutex PR in ~30m. If Alex re-runs CI successfully, we can proceed with the cut. If not, I'll request a hotfix backport path.
deploy-bot: deploy-status: release/train-1842 -> rollout started, 3/5 canaries healthy, next batch in 8m.
Alex: Noted. Blockers: the flaky test + waiting on one approval for #452. Today's plan: triage test, land mutex fix, get Tina's review on #452, and proceed with cut if canaries stay healthy.
Tina: Reviewing #452 now. ETA 20m.
